similarities.label: Similarities
similarities.when: to show two things are alike

phrases.t: They have a great deal in common, namely …

phrases.connector: …, so it is fair to say that …

phrases.t: What they both have in common is …
There is a clear parallel between … and …
phrases.connector: …, since both …, and as a result …

phrases.t: Neither of them was very different.
Either you get this one or that one.

similarities.convention: Both / neither / either / each govern singular and plural agreement differently — a frequent Use of English item as well as a writing error.

tasks.question: What do city life and country life have in common?

cues.cue: city life / country life / offer community
models: Both city life and country life share a strong sense of community, which suggests that people value belonging everywhere, and therefore social bonds matter in both settings.

cues.cue: city life / country life / need / strong local services
models: What city life and country life have in common is a need for strong local services, and this matters because residents everywhere rely on them.

cues.cue: city dwellers / country dwellers / value / green spaces
models: Similarly, both city dwellers and country dwellers value green spaces, which reinforces the idea that access to nature matters to everyone.

cues.cue: city life / country life / offer / a sense of routine
models: There is a clear parallel between city life and country life, since both offer a sense of routine, and as a result people can build stable lives in either.

cues.cue: city / countryside / depend / on transport links
models: In the same vein, both the city and the countryside depend on transport links, so it is fair to say that connectivity matters everywhere.

cues.cue: urban / rural areas / face / rising living costs
models: Correspondingly, urban and rural areas both face rising living costs, which points to a shared economic pressure across the country.

tasks.question: In what ways are online learning and classroom learning alike?

cues.cue: online / classroom learning / need discipline
models: What online learning and classroom learning have in common is that both need discipline, and this matters because success depends on the student's own effort.

cues.cue: online / classroom learning / share / clear learning goals
models: Both online learning and classroom learning share clear learning goals, which suggests that structure matters regardless of format, and therefore students benefit either way.

cues.cue: online / classroom / require / regular practice
models: Similarly, both online and classroom learning require regular practice, which reinforces the idea that consistency drives progress.

cues.cue: online students / classroom students / need / feedback
models: Just as classroom students need feedback, so too do online students, which highlights the fact that guidance matters in every setting.

cues.cue: online courses / classroom courses / also / assess progress through tests
models: Like classroom courses, online courses also assess progress through tests, and this common ground means both aim to track real learning.

cues.cue: online / classroom learning / demand / time management
models: There is a clear parallel between online and classroom learning, since both demand strong time management, and as a result students must plan carefully either way.

tasks.question: What do reading and travelling have in common as ways of learning?

cues.cue: reading / travelling / broaden the mind
models: In much the same way as travelling, reading broadens the mind, and this parallel shows that new experiences, whether real or imagined, expand our understanding.

cues.cue: reading / travelling / share / the power to inspire curiosity
models: Both reading and travelling share the power to inspire curiosity, which suggests that exposure to new ideas matters, and therefore both are valuable forms of learning.

cues.cue: reading / travelling / introduce / us to different perspectives
models: Similarly, reading and travelling both introduce us to different perspectives, which reinforces the idea that learning goes beyond the classroom.

cues.cue: books / journeys / offer / an escape from routine
models: Correspondingly, books and journeys both offer an escape from routine, which points to a shared human need for discovery.

cues.cue: reading / travelling / expose / us to unfamiliar cultures
models: They have a great deal in common, namely that both expose us to unfamiliar cultures, and this is significant because it builds empathy and understanding.

cues.cue: reading / travelling / encourage / independent thinking
models: There is a clear parallel between reading and travelling, since both encourage independent thinking, and as a result learners grow more open-minded through either.

tasks.question: In what ways are TV and social media similar?

cues.cue: TV / social media / entertain / people
models: Similarly, both TV and social media entertain people, which reinforces the idea that people seek out screens for enjoyment as well as information.

cues.cue: TV / social media / share / the ability to spread news quickly
models: Both TV and social media share the ability to spread news quickly, which suggests that speed of information matters to audiences, and therefore both compete for attention.

cues.cue: TV / social media / also / shape public opinion
models: Like TV, social media also shapes public opinion, and this common ground means both carry real influence over how people think.

cues.cue: TV / social media / rely / on advertising
models: What TV and social media have in common is that both rely heavily on advertising, and this matters because content is often driven by commercial interests.

cues.cue: television / social platforms / offer / round-the-clock content
models: Correspondingly, television and social platforms both offer round-the-clock content, which points to a shared drive to keep audiences constantly engaged.

cues.cue: TV / social media / attract / younger and older viewers alike
models: In the same vein, both TV and social media attract younger and older viewers alike, so it is fair to say that screen-based entertainment appeals across generations.

tasks.question: What do all successful students seem to have in common?

cues.cue: successful students / work hard
models: There is a clear parallel between all successful students, since both work hard and manage their time well, and as a result they consistently achieve good results.

cues.cue: successful students / share / strong self-discipline
models: Successful students share strong self-discipline, which suggests that motivation matters as much as ability, and therefore habits often determine outcomes.

cues.cue: successful students / stay / organised
models: What successful students have in common is that they stay organised, and this matters because planning reduces stress before exams.

cues.cue: successful students / set / clear goals
models: Similarly, successful students set clear goals, which reinforces the idea that direction shapes effort.

cues.cue: successful students / seek / help when needed
models: They have a great deal in common, namely that they seek help when needed, and this is significant because asking questions accelerates learning.

cues.cue: top students / manage / their time carefully
models: Correspondingly, top students manage their time carefully, which points to a shared habit of prioritising study over distractions.

tasks.question: In what ways are studying abroad and studying at home alike?

cues.cue: studying abroad / studying at home / share / the goal of academic success
models: Both studying abroad and studying at home share the goal of academic success, which suggests that the destination matters less than the effort, and therefore both paths can lead to good results.

cues.cue: studying abroad / at home / require / self-motivation
models: What studying abroad and studying at home have in common is that both require self-motivation, and this matters because no environment guarantees success on its own.

cues.cue: studying abroad / at home / involve / exam pressure
models: Similarly, studying abroad and studying at home both involve exam pressure, which reinforces the idea that stress is part of academic life everywhere.

cues.cue: students abroad / students at home / also / need strong support networks
models: Like students studying at home, students abroad also need strong support networks, and this common ground means social connection matters wherever you study.

cues.cue: students abroad / students at home / need / good study habits
models: Just as students at home need good study habits, so too do students abroad, which highlights the fact that discipline matters regardless of location.

cues.cue: studying abroad / at home / demand / financial planning
models: Correspondingly, studying abroad and studying at home both demand financial planning, which points to a shared practical challenge facing every student.
